108	- [[cryosoft-project]] — PyQt6 instrument-agnostic cryostat measurement system on OneDrive; parallel worktree sessions, HTTPS remote, agent-ready harness, resources/ for deliverables (hub note)

119	- [[worktree-delegate-review-workflow]] — Sonnet agents implement in a worktree with no-commit; lead agent reviews every diff and owns robustness; waves land only with make check green, committed early

124	### Thesis Writing & Literature Management
125	- [[thesis-literature-workflow]] — library-only citations during writing, research loop separate from writing loop, CrossRef as metadata ground truth, greenfield rebuild preference, stage-by-stage verification, brief from measured-results thesis not the abstract
126	- [[zotero-integration-conventions]] — local API read-only; web API for writes; shared group 11251; dedup is the main failure mode; NEVER /lit-export on CrSBr (textbooks break); inbox key ZSTQMD6T for journal club
127	- [[literature-pdf-grab-via-chrome-cdp]] — lit-grab fetches paywalled PDFs by attaching to a human-launched Chrome over CDP (Cloudflare blocks headless); JGU is VPN-IP based (Nature title-limited + Shibboleth); validate %PDF; lit-grab kept separate from lit-add

130	- [[bulk-ingest-fanout-serial-writer]] — bulk lit ingest: ~72 Sonnet agents write 4 fragments each to tmp (no agent touches vault), one serial ingest_apply.py writes, coverage report is the gate, PDF-only fallback when Zotero offline
131	- [[cross-project-paper-ingestion]] — papers in multiple collections: project membership as a tag for Obsidian Bases filtering, additive no-clobber Relevance, give the ingest agent the citing paper's PDF

136	- [[group-digitization-project]] — co-led (w/ Kilian Leutner) privacy-preserving RAG suite for AG Kläui; data stays in JGU, LLM via KI-Chat-as-MCP, source-traceability mandatory; restructured 2026-06-24 off OneDrive into independent subproject repos under Desktop\P_Projects (hub note)

142	### Learning & Side Projects
143	- [[learn-german-app-conventions]] — German irregular-verb quiz app: no auto-advance, no over-repeat, localStorage persistence, tricky distractors; verb list in Obsidian note; parallel agents for bulk generation

145	### Career & Job Applications
146	- [[cv-honest-skill-bridging]] — never overclaim photonics/optoelectronics (base skill is magnonics/spintronics); bridge from real experience and name both the JD term and the real source, never silently substitute
147	- [[cv-factual-constraints]] — fixed CV/cover-letter facts: no driving licence (flag if a role requires it), don't name the MSc supervisor (Bedanta), PhD only in Experience not Education
148	- [[job-search-platforms-germany]] — German-first job discovery (StepStone/LinkedIn/Indeed.de) + LLM prose-fit scoring (AI Job Finder/Teal/Huntr, CareerBoom.ai for DE); US aggregators thin on DE; keep CV single-column for parsers; EU AI Act Aug-2026 screening disclosure

150	### Infrastructure & Troubleshooting
151	- [[openwebui-ki-chat-gotchas]] — JGU group-digitalization: Native tool-call mode, trycloudflare firewall, OpenAPI servers field; mcpo→cloudflared bridge to plug MCP into KI-Chat; no VS Code dev tunnels
152	- [[jgu-ki-chat-api]] — JGU's OpenAI-compatible KI-Chat LLM API: base URL, fussy exact model ids (verify /models), rate limits, litellm wiring; preferred over Gemini for demos
153	- [[uv-onedrive-hardlink-gotcha]] — uv under OneDrive fails with Windows error 396 (hardlinks); set UV_LINK_MODE=copy (permanent user env var) or pass --link-mode=copy
154	- [[jgu-workstation-ssh]] — group GPU workstation laufey.physik.uni-mainz.de: SSHGATE jump host, three-tier filesystem (/data/aditya fast/local vs NFS home), data taxonomy (pipeline corpus vs resources), scp absolute paths required

158	- [[windows-console-unicode-stdout]] — non-ASCII script output throws UnicodeEncodeError on the cp1252 Windows console; set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 and write to a file; use python -m pip over bare pip
159	- [[scoop-not-winget]] — prefer scoop over winget for Windows CLI installs (winget leaves binaries off PATH); scoop installs may still need a terminal restart before the command resolves
160	- [[onedrive-parallel-session-hazards]] — repos in OneDrive + parallel sessions: files revert mid-task (commit early per stage), deliverables to main tracked resources/, close OneDrive to delete worktrees, find hangs (use Glob)
161	- [[git-worktree-fallthrough-hazard]] — hollow/deleted worktrees make git silently operate on the main checkout; check .git + worktree list; EnterWorktree(path) after manual add; re-verify stale branches against main

# Claude Knowledge Base — Index

Claude's own personalized knowledge base: a plain-markdown, Obsidian-openable vault
of the user's preferences and deep, specific knowledge of the tools and workflows
they actually use. **Separate from the user's research vault. Never merged with it.**

This file is the **routing table**, loaded at the start of every `/kb-update` run so
the agent can decide which notes to read without reading the whole KB. One sharp line
per note, grouped by domain. See `MAINTENANCE.md` for the rules; `NOTE_TEMPLATE.md`
for the note schema.

How to read this KB outside Claude: open the `~/.claude/kb/` folder as a vault in
Obsidian. The `[[slug]]` links render as a graph.

---

## Notes by domain

### Claude Code & Automation
- [[personal-kb-system]] — intent and design of this KB and the /kb-update consolidation skill (hub note)
- [[session-end-habit-no-clear]] — user closes sessions instead of /clear; process on-disk transcripts, never rely on SessionEnd hooks
- [[model-cost-consciousness]] — fan bulk reading out to Haiku/sub-agents, reserve strong models for synthesis, batch expensive work
- [[claude-code-automation-limits]] — hooks can't invoke Claude; subagents can't spawn subagents; only a main agent fans out
- [[subagent-persona-quality-gate]] — user asks for a domain-expert persona sub-agent (e.g. "a German teacher") to QA generated content before finalizing
- [[bash-cwd-resets-mid-session]] — Bash tool resets working dir between calls (pass explicit absolute paths); also single-quote Windows paths since Git Bash eats unquoted backslashes; PowerShell tool is unavailable here
- [[mcp-server-per-project-config]] — Claude Code loads .mcp.json only from the launch dir (not /add-dir); enable a project MCP via .mcp.json + enabledMcpjsonServers/enableAllProjectMcpServers + mcp__x__* allowlist; shared Blender MCP install at developer\blender_mcp\mcp
- [[claude-dir-git-tracked]] — ~/.claude is a git repo (opt-in allowlist) with a PostToolUse auto-commit hook
- [[claude-md-editing-conventions]] — global CLAUDE.md edits: principle numbers are load-bearing (never renumber), additions paid for by cuts, persona/prompt tropes rejected, every-session rules promote KB→CLAUDE.md
- [[context-handoff-doc]] — recovers a lost/polluted context from a written handoff (conclusion paragraph + docs to read + sections to edit); compacts deliberately before a focused edit
- [[permission-scope-discipline]] — global ~/.claude/settings.json stays thin; project rules in project; WebFetch globally allowed; three folder trust-tiers (bypass / accept-edits / always-ask)
- [[minimize-permission-prompts]] — match the allowlist's exact form (tool + literal path); prefer allowlistable fixed scripts over python -c; /fewer-permission-prompts for batch cleanup; PS has no read-only auto-allow
- [[scope-guard-hook]] — PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write/NotebookEdit; silent allow inside cwd + kb + CLAUDE.md, ask everywhere else; tripwire vs prompt injection; BUT fails open (inactive) in PowerShell-less envs like the automated C--WINDOWS-system32 runs
- [[vscode-diff-popup-useterminal]] — VSCode panel diff-approval is a built-in UX layer the allowlist can't silence; `claudeCode.useTerminal:true` is the only escape
- [[link-verification-real-browser]] — verify links by navigating in a real logged-in Chrome (lit-grab CDP), not HTTP: bot 404/403/999 ≠ dead, LLMs fabricate URLs from titles, only emit verbatim tool-result links; PreToolUse hooks fire for sub-agent Write/Edit
- [[skill-placement-project-vs-global]] — project-tied skills go in <project>/.claude/skills/; only zero-project-assumption cross-project skills go global; ONLY .claude/skills/ is auto-discovered (legacy SKILLs/ retired); when unsure, ask
- [[agent-doc-mirrors-sync]] — Workspace CLAUDE.md is mirrored to AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md; edit only CLAUDE.md and regenerate mirrors via scripts/sync_agent_docs.py
- [[git-track-before-editing]] — add a file to git before editing it; tracking is the per-file reversibility safety net ("add the manuscript to git, then edit")
- [[git-workflow-preferences]] — SSH transport (not HTTPS), ed25519 key at gitlab.rlp.net/@kuaditya, rebase before push when remote diverges (not merge), CLAUDE.md carries canonical remote URL
- [[writing-quality-gates]] — two-gate manuscript QA: deterministic linter (zero false positives, [LINTABLE]) + semantic /sci-review ([REVIEWER]); hook-fired; sci-write/sci-review now two separate composing skills (see [[sci-write-skill-architecture]])
- [[capture-workflow-as-skill]] — once a multi-step workflow is proven, codify it as a reusable (git-tracked) project skill ("write a skill on how to compile the manuscript PDF")
- [[oracle-before-automation]] — ask "do you have a pass/fail oracle?" before designing any automated QA loop; inventory existing tools first before new infrastructure
- [[exploration-session-defaults]] — learning/exploration CLAUDE.md must declare read-only default mode; scope = directory intent, not code contents; multi-repo workspaces need explicit authority statements
- [[local-scheduling-not-cloud-agents]] — recurring jobs that touch local files (vault/morning-digest) run on Windows Task Scheduler + local `claude` CLI, NOT cloud agents (cloud can't see local paths); 7 AM digest skill staged via outbox
- [[chrome-terminal-vs-sidebar]] — Claude-in-Chrome has two modes: toolbar = standalone sidebar app (wrong); `/chrome` = terminal CLI session drives the browser (what the user wants); backs the LinkedIn scrape
- [[skill-description-token-budget]] — always-loaded context (skill descriptions, CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md) is a per-session token tax; keep descriptions terse and audit for bloat (2,200→1,840-word trim)
- [[autonomy-obvious-vs-working-style]] — from a batch of proposed changes: just-implement the obvious/low-risk ones, ask only about changes that affect the user's working style (the cut line is working-style impact, not size)
- [[per-project-effort-level]] — default reasoning effort set per project via `effortLevel` in settings.local.json; PhD-Thesis runs xhigh; CrSBr turned down from xhigh to medium 2026-07-26 (check current value, don't assume); `/effort` still overrides per-turn
- [[agent-operable-tooling-design]] — tools agents drive: one-shot CLI (no REPL), read/write subcommand split for allowlist gating, JSON transcripts, expertise in static artifacts, contracts as trust wall, safe hardware excitation
- [[cross-machine-session-tracing]] — git commits carry no session id (no Co-Authored-By trailer); trace a commit to its Claude session by branch + timestamp window over local transcripts, not metadata

### Working Style & Scientific Practice
- [[sci-write-skill-architecture]] — two-layer writing standard (generic skill + project GLOSSARY.md §6); sci-write = final-stage conversion only; sci-review = adversarial audit; no GLOSSARY, no draft
- [[knowledge-as-linked-graph]] — user reasons in linked atomic notes; keep Claude's KB separate from the research vault
- [[collaboration-dialectic-style]] — reason before drafting; designs in forcing arguments (forced vs optional); expects push-back not affirmation (stated, codified as CLAUDE.md Principle 10); wants formal design docs (Amodei-style) not blog essays; companion docs for implementation details
- [[objective-progress-report-style]] — report results objectively first; decisive chi^2/DOF model comparison; honest tension tables
- [[multi-source-research-synthesis]] — consolidate figures+data before writing; fan out paper extraction to sub-agents; attribute precisely
- [[scientific-model-selection]] — for scientific ML (embeddings/LLMs), pick a domain-appropriate model (SPECTER2 etc.) and justify it; don't default to the convenient generic one
- [[result-first-narrative]] — physics prose "reverse logic": plan the one-paragraph story, then lead with the observed result and explain it; don't open from theory or another paper's prediction
- [[progress-report-interpretation-split]] — two companion docs: objective progress report (withholds interpretation) + versioned interpretation_and_placement doc (physics + lit placement, dated retractions by symbol)
- [[figure-plan-and-economy]] — panel-by-panel figure plan before/with drafting; main text carries only claim-making panels, raw data + non-winning fits go to SI
- [[manuscript-revision-conventions]] — revision pass: extract reviewer PDF via pdf-comments first, clean narrow context, copy V_n→V_{n+1} and edit there, freeze dated baseline for latexdiff, SI-before-main, stage-don't-commit, triage findings (safe-auto vs hold-for-user), verify numbers against notebooks, soften to open-questions framing, prune weak citations, minimal spec-driven figure edits, condense long plans into a physics-only summary doc
- [[physics-explanation-style]] — to learn a physics concept he wants a professor-style one-on-one that builds an intuitive mental picture in layers, pitched at grad level; recommendations first, not questions
- [[manuscript-single-model-consistency]] — manuscript commits to ONE physical model stated identically across abstract/figures/captions/SI; defensive detail parked out; Opus reviewer hunts inconsistencies; reject terms experiment can't justify
- [[manuscript-open-points-honesty]] — state uncertainty as explicit open points (mandated O1-O5 sentences + plan gate); every model stays in its regime (R6); honest incompleteness over a fitted complete picture
- [[house-style-corpus-mining]] — derive house writing style empirically from the PI's (Kläui) 100+ paper corpus (last-author subset); overselling-detection is top priority; adversarially verify rules don't flag his own abstracts
- [[glossary-source-of-truth]] — GLOSSARY.md is the canonical authority for notation/terminology/canonical values; a decision not reflected there isn't finished; preserve canonical values when editing prose; glossary_reminder.py hook
- [[deep-research-prompt-conventions]] — deep-research prompts: name the material to anchor scope, concrete sub-questions not "explain the reasoning", structure by conceptual level + paper type, always a conflation/disagreement section
- [[answer-before-editing]] — when a request bundles a question with an edit, answer first and wait; don't edit the manuscript in the same turn as the explanation
- [[collaborator-email-conventions]] — collaborator emails are formal-academic, lead with the technical concerns + venue; co-author sections stay as visible italic bracketed placeholders that must render in the sent PDF
- [[llm-draft-cross-check]] — external LLM drafts (Gemini etc.) are untrusted hypotheses: verify the reasoning/math not just facts, verify links live, structure short+long, stage via outbox before adopting into the vault
- [[optimize-for-user-review-bottleneck]] — user is the throughput bottleneck ("fasten the bottleneck time, that is me"): visual interactive HTML for system design (custom tooling over Artifacts), extractive-learnings not status for reviews
- [[direct-not-oversimplified-scientific-prose]] — "direct" = cut preamble, keep normal subordination (rejected an overcorrected draft as "high school writing"); claim ladder, drop unsupported machinery, flatten embedded questions, offer numbered rewrite alternatives
- [[code-cites-standards-not-plans]] — CLAUDE.md Rule 5: no `plan §`/`docs/plans/` citations in code (they rot; agent-commit failure mode); vendor manual `§` refs stay; archive superseded plans with status banners; enforced by a conformance test, not agent diligence
- [[finish-dont-revert-half-swept-changes]] — a half-swept sweep (touched but not finished) is worse than either extreme; finish it rather than reverting once real edits exist there
- [[preserve-structure-when-editing]] — editing the user's own drafts (institutional emails) is surgical: keep their language/structure, fix only accuracy/grammar, don't rewrite

### Jupyter, Plotting & LaTeX
- [[scientific-figure-conventions]] — figsize 6x5, dpi 300 (not 600), Okabe-Ito, no titles, adjacent AFM/FM subplots, --o for sparse; multi-panel grids: per-row y-limits (not global sharey), strip repeated labels, χ² annotated in-panel
- [[figure-composite-assembly-pipeline]] — modular per-panel PNGs tiled by scripts/figuregen/assemble_composites.py (layout = one line edit), auto-backup to _originals_before_replace/, redrawn from binned per-T CSVs, per-version v2/v3 dirs, keep standalone figures
- [[notebook-build-workflow]] — build notebooks via Python/nbformat (run: nbconvert --execute kernel data_analysis); tmp copies; edit oversized via JSON; additive idempotent edits + .BEFORE_insert backup; don't auto-run composite-rebuilding notebooks; collapsed cells (source_hidden ignored by VS Code); paste-able code for single-cell iteration
- [[latex-manuscript-conventions]] — math-mode bib subscripts, upright \mathrm{} label-subscript house style (apply to main + \input'd SI), biber-direct, provenance tags for /verify-references, fig_/figS_ naming, openwork.sty titlesec hides section numbers (override \titleformat in body)
- [[latexdiff-review-windows]] — review manuscript edits as a latexdiff --flatten PDF off a frozen dated baseline; Windows MiKTeX fix: vendor pure-Perl Algorithm::Diff (Diff.pm) into latexdiff's script dir
- [[crystal-schematic-skill]] — ASE + matplotlib for atomic structure figures; VESTA rejected (closed CLI, template-only); Okabe-Ito atoms, top+side, ~3×3 supercell
- [[blender-mcp-conventions]] — render-and-verify mandatory; renders to tmp/blender-mcp/{ts}/ via scene.render.filepath; Cycles+denoise (EEVEE preview); Standard view transform; ortho+transparent; ASE+procedural atoms (not Beautiful Atoms); 3D-only, 2D diagrams stay matplotlib insets; vector labels never baked
- [[figure-physical-fidelity]] — manuscript schematics must show the real mechanism grounded in the source paper's figure (read the PDF, verify orbital/structure first); generic cartoons rejected; offer candidate variants to output/
- [[afm-plot-conventions]] — AFM topography figures: afmhot colormap, plane-level + substrate-zero, side-by-side line scan for flake step height; Bruker .000 header parsing

### Obsidian
- [[obsidian-cli-windows-gotchas]] — call obsidian.com not .exe, gate on stdout (exit 255 on success), native `obsidian file` resolver; do NOT write note bodies via `create content=` (crashes >4KB, mangles LaTeX, silent truncation) — use the filesystem helper; CLI fine for reads + small property:set
- [[obsidian-tooling-choices]] — official Obsidian CLI first; aaronsb MCP plugin for graph traversal; localhost-only, "Allow once"; global obsidian skills live in ~/.claude/skills/ and depend on obsidian-core (cli-recipes hub)
- [[obsidian-vault-write-architecture]] — vault writes go through ONE audited filesystem helper (stage_to_outbox.py/apply.py) into the outbox, byte-exact atomic — NOT the CLI content= (unsafe) nor the agent's Write tool; narrow permission surface; never edit live notes or invent missing data
- [[obsidian-vault-schema-conventions]] — house style: singular category names, lowercase casing (status/birthday), property `type` not `kind`, schema under 07 Schema/Templates/; fix obvious formatting without asking
- [[obsidian-templater-conventions]] — Templater over core Templates; tp.file.move() auto-routes notes by template; date autofill migrated off core (didn't work w/ Templater); preserve hand-crafted templates, skip BetterBibTeX Jinja2
- [[vault-bulk-edit-review-discipline]] — bulk vault/template edits: frontmatter-only pass, test on a few notes (only intended field changes), enumerate edge cases, dry-run, review every diff, then apply
- [[obsidian-skill-output-conventions]] — Obsidian retrieve skills write digest + raw notes to the CALLING project's tmp/, not the skill dir; preserve raw [[links]]; don't pre-build a dup-name index

content.text:
Six spectra fall into three groups: B and D are sharp and bulk-like, C and E are broad and degraded-looking, and A and F are intermediate. I've only run the QC and the multi-spectrum fit so far. I haven't run the per-band refit, opened the literature figures, or built the notebook.

All six show the CrSBr room-temperature signature, so the material is not in question. The three Ag modes are near 108 to 114, 238 to 244 and 340 to 343 cm⁻¹. QC found no spikes or saturation. The 50 to 431 cm⁻¹ window has no Si line, so I could not check calibration.

| | Ag1 (cm⁻¹) | Ag3 position (cm⁻¹) | Ag3 FWHM (cm⁻¹) | Ag2/Ag3 height | 302 cm⁻¹ band |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 108.3 (FWHM 9) | 341.1 | 6.7 | 0.08 | very weak |
| B | 114.0 (FWHM 3.6) | 342.9 | 3.8 | 0.43 | absent |
| C | no sharp peak, broad hump ~99 (FWHM ~65) | 340.9 | 6.7 | ~0.15, redshifted to 237.6 | 0.20 |
| D | 113.3 (FWHM 4.1) | 341.5 / 343.2 | 4.1 / 2.7 | 0.19 | absent |
| E | broad hump ~99 (FWHM ~68) | 340.2 | 6.9 | ~0.15, near 238 | 0.21 |
| F | 111.9 (FWHM 4.6) | 340.6 | 5.4 | 0.39 | ~0.01 |

- **B and D** have narrow lines, a sharp Ag1 at 113 to 114 cm⁻¹, no 302 cm⁻¹ band and no broad background. This matches the "sharp Lorentzian Ag modes, no D1/D3" quality criterion in the CrSBr notes (Torres 2022, arXiv 2212.01754, Fig. 2).
- **A** has a clearly redshifted Ag1 (108 cm⁻¹, about 5 to 6 cm⁻¹ below B and D) and a very weak Ag2. Ag1 and Ag2 are the thickness-sensitive modes, and Ag1 redshifts as layers decrease (Torres 2022, Fig. 1h). So A is probably the thinnest flake of the six. Confidence: moderate.
- **C and E** have no sharp Ag1. Instead there is a broad hump near 80 to 105 cm⁻¹. The Ag3 line is broadened to ~7 cm⁻¹, Ag2 is weak and shifted to ~238 cm⁻¹, and a 302 cm⁻¹ band is clearly present. The notes tie D1 (a shoulder 5 to 10 cm⁻¹ below Ag1) and D* (a broad band at 90 to 100 cm⁻¹) to air exposure or damage (Torres 2022, p.4-5). This looks like a degraded or defective surface, and E looks worse than C. Whether it is degradation or just thin flakes is not settled by these data. Confidence: low to moderate.
- **F** sits between the others: Ag1 at 111.9 cm⁻¹ and Ag3 FWHM of 5.4 cm⁻¹.

I could not check these items, so don't lean on them:
- **Ag3 position:** it should be nearly layer-independent (about 344 cm⁻¹ per Torres 2022), yet it spans 340.2 to 342.9 cm⁻¹ here. That 2.7 cm⁻¹ spread is not thickness. It could be calibration drift, strain, or fit artifacts. Without a Si line I can't tell which.
- **Ag2/Ag3 ratio:** at 532 nm the Ag2 intensity depends strongly on polarization relative to the a and b axes (Mondal 2025, arXiv 2410.22164, Fig. 3), and on interference for thick flakes. I don't know your polarization geometry, so this ratio is not a reliable thickness indicator here.
- **Weak-band tracking:** the multi-spectrum fit gave inconsistent results for weak bands such as the 98 cm⁻¹ hump and the 240 cm⁻¹ band. Those entries are low confidence until the per-band refit in the notebook.
- **Layer number:** Raman shifts alone don't give it (Ye 2022, ACS Nano 16, 11876). The A-versus-B/D ordering is only a ranking. AFM or optical contrast would settle it.

To firm this up, I need three things from you: the polarization geometry and angle to the a/b axes, whether you have AFM or contrast thickness for these flakes, and the substrate (I assumed SiO₂/Si).

I can also run the per-band refit, check the literature figures, and build the Marimo notebook. Say if you want that.
